issue.title: rust-dev-install replaces sase_core_rs non-atomically, so concurrent imports SIGBUS or miss the module
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-1tz.3.1.2 (swap_repro, epic sase-1tz.3.1) as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #4; filed by the sase-1tz.3.1 land agent.

`maturin develop` (used by the Justfile `rust-dev-install*` recipes, which `sase dev update` runs as the reconcile step "Rebuild Rust dev artifacts into the uv-tool venv", `src/sase/dev_update/_plan_reconcile.py:101,112`, and `src/sase/mode_switch/plan.py:273`) deletes the previous `sase_core_rs.abi3.so`, then copies about 60 MB into the final path. A process that imports the binding mid-copy either finds no module (ModuleNotFoundError) or maps a short file and dies of SIGBUS (exit -7). The swap_repro reproducer models this in `tests/dev_update/test_swap_repro_native.py::test_mapping_a_partially_copied_file_sigbuses_past_its_end`.

Field evidence (sase-1tz.3.1.2 notes #2, #3): all 6 SIGBUS exits on athena and apollo in the 7 days before 2026-11-20 started while a writer was live, inside that rebuild step. By contrast, the prebuild consumer (`src/sase/dev_update/prebuild_consumer.py`, `_copy_atomic`) already writes a temp file and renames it.

The swap guards from sase-1tz.3.1.3 and .4 keep scheduler jobs and launches from starting during a swap. Readers that no guard sees, such as ad-hoc CLI invocations and the TUI, still hit the copy window.

Fix: build or copy the extension to a staging path in the same directory and rename it into place, as `_copy_atomic` does. The same applies to the uv-tool variant. Read the `tools.md` reference memory if this touches `tools/`. After install, confirm with `tools/swap_overlap_census --days 7 --tz America/New_York --details` that the sigbus and missing_binding rows stay at 0.
